Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Daga,Vipul Raj Gautam
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Chhaya Gupta,Sujeet Kumar

Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant-accused, Sri Amrendra Nath Singh, learned Senior Advocate, assisted by Sri Sujeet Kumar for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in case crime No.08 of 2022,
under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 376 I.P.C. and section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Kotwali, District Prayagraj with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant-accused that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is brother-in-law (dever) of informant/prosecutrix.
The marriage of informant with brother of applicant-accused has taken place on 21.11.2019.
The allegations regarding harassment of informant made against applicant-accused, are thoroughly false and baseless.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was Vaibhav Jain vs State Of U.P.

1 submitted that the allegations of informant that applicant-accused has committed rape upon her,
are thoroughly improbable.
Only vague allegation has been made that applicant forcibly established physical relations with her and no specific date and time of alleged incident was mentioned.
The informant has even gone to the extent and made allegation of rape against her father-in-law.

Learned counsel has pointed out a hand written note of informant, which is annexed as Annexure-17, wherein, she has mentioned that in future she would never indulge in fighting with the family of her in-laws and she has said sorry to her father-in-law and sought pardon.
She has also mentioned that she would live in the house of her in-laws peacefully and would not make undue interference.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that in fact the behavior of the informant was not proper.
It was also pointed out that the informant and her family members have concealed the fact before marriage that her gallbladder has already been removed.
Further, she used to create scenes at the house of her in-laws and in the year 2020 during COVID-19 pandemic, she has also made an attempt to cut her veins.

Due to all these facts, the husband of informant has filed a petition under Section 12 Hindu Marriage Act for declaration of the marriage as void and after that first information report of this case was lodged on 15.01.2022, making false and baseless allegations.
Lastly, it has been submitted that the applicant-accused is languishing in jail since 06.11.2022,
having no criminal history and that in case, the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.
Learned A.G.A. as well as learned Senior Counsel have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that there are allegations of rape against applicant.

Referring to statement of informant, it was submitted that the informant was continuously harassed by the applicant and his family members and she was subjected to cruelty and that applicant has committed rape upon her.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that there are serious allegations against applicant-accused.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant-accused Vaibhav Jain involved in aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned
subject to following conditions:
1. The applicant-accused shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The applicant-accused shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The applicant-accused shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The applicant-accused shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

sentences.text: 5. The applicant-accused shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant-accused in accordance with law.
